source_revalidation.finding: The donor already registers wildcard PreToolUse and PostToolUse hooks through stern.py, while dedicated SubagentStart/SubagentStop/TaskCreated/TaskCompleted hooks are absent.
A direct exact-source search finds no agent_id handling in stern.py, so the current donor does not persist or use subagent identity from hook payloads even if the runtime supplies it.

source_revalidation.source: Claude Code official hooks documentation observed 2026-08-28
source_revalidation.finding: Plugin/settings hooks also run for tool calls made inside subagents, and common hook input carries agent_id and agent_type when the hook executes inside a subagent. PostToolUse carries call-scoped tool_use_id. This does not prove the installed target version or exact Agent parent-tool response schema.

refined_design: Do not require dedicated SubagentStart/SubagentStop hooks merely to obtain child identity on child tool calls: first reuse the already-configured PreToolUse/PostToolUse path and preserve observed agent_id, agent_type and tool_use_id as typed evidence fields.
Extend stern.py/common hook admission so optional agent_id and agent_type are never silently dropped. Their absence remains UNKNOWN, not parent identity and not a fabricated child identity.
Dedicated SubagentStart/SubagentStop remains useful for lifecycle boundaries, child-without-tool cases and transcript continuity, but is not the only possible source of agent_id evidence.
This refinement improves child tool/effect attribution after an agent is identified, but it does not close the durable workpackage_id -> parent Agent invocation -> child agent_id causal join.

The parent-to-child join still requires an observed immutable shared key, a deliberately injected nonce, or a wrapper receipt. Timing, event order, session_id and narration remain forbidden join methods.
task_id stays an independent optional task-system identity and must never be substituted for agent_id.
architecture_refinement.unknown_preservation: Missing agent_id/agent_type/task_id or parent-child join evidence remains explicit UNKNOWN and cannot receive native-child execution credit.

contradiction_refinement.current_statement: The versioned donor lacks dedicated native child lifecycle hooks and stern.py does not ingest agent_id, but the configured wildcard tool hooks may already receive agent_id/agent_type for child tool calls under current Claude Code semantics. Therefore child tool identity capture is a smaller repair than full lifecycle invention, while deterministic workpackage-to-spawn-to-agent binding remains unproven.

counterhypotheses: The installed target Claude Code build may not match current documented hook payload semantics; source adaptation must remain optional-field tolerant until exact target payloads are observed.
A host-private lifecycle hook or wrapper may already close workpackage-to-agent binding; if observed, import/adapt it rather than creating duplicate authority.
The Agent parent tool_response may contain a stable child identifier, making a nonce/wrapper unnecessary; this remains unproven until exact target payload evidence exists.

feeds_triggerword_4.source_ready_change: Add optional child identity preservation to the existing tool-hook admission path and unit-test absent/present/mismatched agent_id fields without granting runtime credit.
feeds_triggerword_4.runtime_discriminator: On an explicitly admitted target runtime lane, capture one non-mutating Agent invocation plus child tool event/lifecycle payloads and prove or falsify an immutable parent invocation -> agent_id join.
feeds_triggerword_4.forbidden_inference: Never join by time proximity, event ordering, session identity or model narration.
